patches.value: For every interval I=[a,b] in [0,infinity), |I|<=1, and mean-zero continuous piecewise smooth functions f1,f2,f3 with finite Xnorm(I), ||Cop_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C|I| product_j||fj||_X(I)+C||fi||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar))) product_(j!=i)||fj||_(L^infinity(I;L2)) for each i=1,2,3. The same estimate holds for arbitrary continuous functions in Xnorm with L^infinity L2 regularity and a distributional time derivative in L^infinity H^(-pstar). For time-independent mean-zero fj in H^sigma, 0<=sigma<=1, ||Cop_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_sigma |I|^sigma product_j||fj||_(H^sigma), interpreted with the bounded extension. Constants are uniform in interval location and Fourier support.

Under the step hypotheses explicitly stated below, with smooth states initially and the interpolation D023, sup_(I_n)||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=C_(M0,gamma) q_n, sup_(I_n)||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C_(M0,gamma) tau q_n, sup_(I_n)||Y_n||_2<=C_(M0,gamma) q_n, ||Y_n||_X(I_n)<=C_(M0,gamma) q_n and sup_(I_n)||Y_n||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(M0,gamma) tau q_n. These estimates are uniform in step and Fourier support. Here explicitly the hypotheses are 0<tau<=1, n>=0, mean-zero f_n in L2 and w in H^gamma, ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 and delta_n=||f_n-w||_2<=1, q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n.

For smooth exact and numerical flows defined in D023 on [0,T] with sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, 0<tau=T/L<=1, let I=[a,b] start at a grid point, h=b-a<=1, E_I=sup_I||v-V||_2<=1. Set e=v-V, g=v-e/2 and F_I(t)=integral_a^t Bop_s(e,g)ds. Then e(t)=e(a)+F_I(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)). For every N>=2, sup_I||P_leq(N)F_I||_2<=C N^2 h E_I and sup_I||P_gt(N)F_I||_2<=C(h+tau)tau^gamma+C(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))E_I. Consequently E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C(h+tau)tau^gamma+C(N^2 h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))E_I. Constants depend only on M0,gamma (and the fixed final horizon) and are uniform in Fourier support, restart a and step size.
